newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says still aims for 20% tax rate.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says still aims for 20% tax rate.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he was still aiming to reduce the standard rate of income tax to 20 percent and would cut taxes again as soon as public finances allowed.

"I have been absolutely clear that my target of taxation is to reach a standard rate of 20 pence in the pound and it will be achieved as long as public finances can afford it," he told a news conference.
Clarke defended the fact that the ruling Conservatives had raised taxes in the first two budgets he presided over.
"Yes, we took tough measures which involved some increases in taxation," he said. "We will continue on that tax cutting agenda when it is sensible to do so."
The standard rate of income tax in Britain is 24 percent, with a starting rate of 20 percent. The top rate is 40 percent.
Clarke said Britain's economy was set for a sustainable recovery with low inflation, low interest rates and rising living standards.
